selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What are the two medicines mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: They are trusting Allah with patience, and relying on Allah’s power while being sure of His wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage describe a person who knows he is weak and turns to Allah?
questions.answer: It describes him as someone who feels safe by depending on the Lord of the whole world.

questions.question: What does a believer say when a very hard trouble comes?
questions.answer: He says that he belongs to Allah and will return to Him.

questions.question: Why does the passage say such a person has less to fear?
questions.answer: Because he trusts Allah’s mercy and power instead of depending only on himself.

questions.question: What surprising idea does the passage teach about weakness and fear of Allah?
questions.answer: It teaches that they can bring a kind of sweetness and peace when they lead a person to Allah.

questions.question: What example is given to help explain this idea?
questions.answer: An example is given of a very young child who feels safest by running to his mother when he feels helpless.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does the kindness of mothers show us?
questions.answer: It shows a small sign of Allah’s much greater mercy.

questions.question: Why did wise people admit that they had no real power of their own?
questions.answer: Because they wanted to seek shelter in Allah and not be fooled by pride.

questions.question: What did wise people make into a means of drawing near to Allah?
questions.answer: They used their weakness and their fear of Allah as a way to turn to Him.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of this passage?
questions.answer: The main lesson is that a person finds peace by knowing his need for Allah and trusting Him fully.

questions.question: In this passage, what is the first medicine made of?
questions.answer: It is made of trust in Allah and patience.

questions.question: What is the second part of the two medicines in this passage?
questions.answer: It is depending on the Creator’s power and trusting His wise plan.

questions.question: How is Allah’s power shown in the passage?
questions.answer: It is shown as unlimited power that can make things happen by His command.

questions.question: When someone faces a disaster, what should he do according to the passage?
questions.answer: He should remember that he belongs to Allah and place his trust in Him.

questions.question: What kind of Lord does the passage tell the believer to trust?
questions.answer: A Lord who is full of compassion and care.

questions.question: Why might a person with knowledge of Allah find comfort even in weakness?
questions.answer: Because weakness helps him stop trusting himself and turn to Allah.

questions.question: What does the baby example teach about fear?
questions.answer: It teaches that fear can lead someone to a place of safety and tenderness.

questions.question: Is the mercy of human mothers the highest mercy described here?
questions.answer: No. It is only a tiny sign of Allah’s much greater mercy.

questions.question: What did wise people do because of this understanding?
questions.answer: They turned away from claiming strength for themselves and sought protection in Allah.

questions.question: What attitude does the passage warn against without saying it directly?
questions.answer: It warns against pride in one’s own strength and acting as if one does not need Allah.

questions.question: What two actions are called medicines in the passage?
questions.answer: Patient trust in Allah, and confidence in Allah’s power and wisdom.

questions.question: According to the passage, what should a person do with his helplessness?
questions.answer: He should use it to rely on Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage answer the question of whether these medicines really help?
questions.answer: It says clearly that they truly do help.

questions.question: Why is a person stronger when he admits his weakness before Allah?
questions.answer: Because he is then supported by Allah instead of being left to his own limited ability.
